group.passage: Every April and May, white Tung flowers cover the hills of northern and central Taiwan, and many visitors travel to see them. Below, an old Hakka farmer remembers what the trees once meant to his family, and a hiker writes about her trip to see the flowers.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: A Farmer Remembers
passage_parts.text: When I was a boy, my family grew Tung trees on the hills behind our village. We did not grow them for their flowers. We grew them for their seeds. We would press the seeds to make Tung oil, which kept water out. People painted it on boats and furniture, and the paper umbrellas made in Meinong needed it too. The wood was useful as well. It was made into furniture and matches. My mother always warned us never to eat the fruit, because it is poisonous. In spring, the falling flowers turned our yard white. Those trees helped many Hakka families make a living. Later, fewer people needed Tung oil, and the trees were no longer worth much. I never imagined that people would one day come from the cities just to look at their flowers.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Hiking Under the “Snow of April”
passage_parts.text: Last Saturday, my friends and I took a train to Miaoli to see the Tung flowers. The trails were busy with families, and almost everyone had a camera. Halfway up the mountain, a light wind began to blow, and white flowers came down all around us. They covered the path like a thin blanket of snow. Now I understand why people call this sight the “snow of April.” Along the trail, we stopped at a small shop run by a Hakka family and tried sweet rice cakes and tea. A sign by the shop said that the Hakka Affairs Council started the Tung Blossom Festival in 2002 to share Hakka culture with visitors. Before I went home, I picked up a fallen flower and pressed it in my notebook. It will remind me of a perfect spring day.

translation_zh.text:
【引言】每年四、五月，白色的桐花開滿台灣北部和中部的山丘，許多遊客專程前往賞花。以下是一位客家老農回憶桐樹曾經對他的家庭代表什麼，以及一位登山客寫下她的賞花之旅。
【A 老農的回憶】我還是個男孩的時候，家裡在村子後面的山坡上種桐樹。我們種桐樹不是為了花，而是為了種子。我們會把種子壓榨成桐油，桐油可以防水。人們把它塗在船和家具上，美濃做的紙傘也要用到它。木材也很有用，可以做成家具和火柴。媽媽總是警告我們絕對不可以吃桐樹的果實，因為它有毒。春天的時候，落下的花把我們的院子染成一片白。那些樹幫助許多客家家庭維持生計。後來，需要桐油的人越來越少，桐樹也就不再值什麼錢了。我從來沒想過，有一天會有人從城市專程來看它們的花。
【B 在「四月雪」下健行】上星期六，我和朋友搭火車到苗栗看桐花。步道上滿是一家大小，幾乎每個人都帶著相機。爬到半山腰時，吹起一陣微風，白色的花在我們四周紛紛落下，像一層薄薄的雪鋪滿了步道。現在我終於明白，為什麼大家把這幅景象叫做「四月雪」。沿著步道，我們在一家客家人開的小店停下來，嚐了甜甜的米糕，喝了茶。店旁的告示牌寫著，客家委員會在 2002 年開始舉辦桐花祭，和遊客分享客家文化。回家之前，我撿起一朵落花，把它壓在筆記本裡。它會讓我記得這個完美的春日。
